chapter: Strings, arrangements and the Shrine band
title: Four saxes at the Jung Hotel and complaints about too much brass
summary: At the Jung Hotel a social leader complained of too much brass when his section was saxophones; DeDroit contrasts the Jung with the Roosevelt.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Oh yeah, sure, sure, sure, sure, sure. You know some people, they'll just get the habit of saying they don't like brass, but they do. But they just want to be with the crowd that doesn't like brass, and they'd say, they don't like brass. But after a while they got impressed on them that they liked it. When I had the contract at the Jung Hotel I had four saxes, and the social leader, she was a social leader too in town, she tried to bring some social life to the Jung, which it never did have. She says, you have too much brass. I said, what brass? I said, those are not brass. I said, those are reed and stones. She thought they were brass because they looked like brass. They were gold. You don't go and play the saxes. And I was a trumpet player, and if it was too loud, I thought it was my fault. Yeah, I know it wasn't too loud. You know? But they have to have some excuse why they can't bring the business in. At the Jung, a fine hotel, fine people, and I went in, picked them away. But they didn't have the social life. The Roosevelt had it. That's the only way it stood.

I played in the Roosevelt. Did you have a roof at the Jung? Sir? Yeah. Can you take, can you do it? Well, we can just keep on talking. Yeah. Sure you have enough. Mrs. Roosevelt? Uh... You ask me the question, sir. Yeah. Um...
